findings.title: Template-name-keyed rules loading is a missed dependency on the "one required code change" claim
findings.description:
The design says `TEMPLATE_INPUTS` is "the one required code change" because the registry is keyed by exact template name. That is not the only name-keyed lookup on the review path. `ReviewAction._review()` calls `load_review_rules(template_name, ...)`, and `get_template_rules` in `review/rules.py` reads `review-{template_name}.md` and `review.md`. A judge named `judge.slice-vs-arch` will not pick up any project rules written for `review-slice.md` or `review-tasks.md`. It will only get the generic `review.md`.

The architecture lists "the project rules" as part of a judge's in-repo ground truth. The judge variants would silently get different rules from the templates whose criteria they claim to mirror. The design's own "naming is not a dispatch signal" decision is also contradicted: rules selection is a second name-keyed dispatch, and the design neither mentions nor handles it. Decide explicitly between:
- documenting that judge templates take only `review.md`;
- adding `review-judge.*.md` rules files; or
- changing the lookup.

Also confirm that the persisted review filename and header, which embed the template name, are acceptable with a dotted name.

findings.title: Structured-output constraint and enforced score-with-rationale are dropped from plan scope
findings.description:
The slice plan entry for 302 assigns two things to this slice:
- "Each template uses a structured-output constraint for the score field."
- "The score-with-rationale shape is enforced by the template's structured output."

The architecture's score-reliability mitigation (b) says the same. The design instead relies on prose instructions, and states that `## Rationale` is "prose scaffolding... not a new parser target". Nothing checks that a rationale is present, and nothing constrains the `score:` field beyond a prompt request. A missing rationale would pass silently, with no log line.

Either:
- state how the template constrains the score field (for example, an explicit output-format block plus the existing `score:` parse), and add an observable signal when `## Rationale` is absent; or
- record explicitly that enforcement is deferred, and why. The plan entry needs updating if so.

findings.title: "Reuse existing criteria" is implemented as copy-paste, which creates the drift the design says it avoids
findings.description:
The design justifies reuse so that "the two should agree on *what* good looks like". The mechanism is "copy the standard template's criteria" into two new YAML files. The existing `slice.yaml` and `tasks.yaml` embed their criteria inside `system_prompt` text. After the copy there are two independent copies, and an edit to `slice.yaml`'s criteria will not reach `judge.slice-vs-arch`.

The design should either name a mechanism that keeps one source of truth, or state that drift is accepted and how it will be detected. For example, a test that asserts the judge criteria block equals the standard template's.

findings.title: Failure-mode table omits ground-truth read failure, injection-cap overflow, and unparseable output
Required-input failure path is correctly mapped and verified
findings.description: The `TEMPLATE_INPUTS` row's handling matches the current code. The required-input check in `_review()` raises `KeyError`, and `_exception_result` re-looks up the template and returns `UNKNOWN` with judge provenance and a WARNING log. The "no new handling code" claim holds for this row. The restated no-silent-pass NFR is consistent with the architecture.

findings.title: Layering, dependency direction and threshold locus match the architecture
findings.description:
- **Engine boundary:** The slice makes no engine change. Judge identity comes from the `judge:` block, not the name.
- **Threshold values:** They live in template YAML with step override, as the architecture requires.
- **Threshold choice:** The values are differentiated by ground-truth strength, which matches "bubble up the hard calls". They are no more permissive than the 75/50 module defaults.
- **Verdict:** The prompt forbids a model-emitted verdict, matching "the judge emits score + findings, not a verdict".
- **Dependencies:** They point only at 301 and 300.

findings.title: Test scope partly duplicates slice 301
findings.description: The "rogue verdict is discarded" test exercises `enforce_judge`, which slice 301 already owns and tests. It can be dropped, or reduced to one parse-then-enforce check using a real raw output with a verdict line. The Risk section also calls the prompt shape "two new I/O paths". A prompt is not an I/O path, so the wording could be tightened.

findings.title: Findings-format contract and CLI invocation need pinning
findings.description:
The design says not to copy the `slice.yaml` CRITICAL verdict-consistency block. It does not say to keep the `### [SEVERITY]` and `location:` finding format, which the parser needs. State that explicitly so the judge prompt does not drop it along with the verdict block.

Success criterion 3 uses `sq review slice-vs-arch <artifact> <against>`, while the walkthrough uses `--template judge.slice-vs-arch`. The design already defers confirming the CLI shape to implementation, but the two forms should be made consistent.

Failure-mode table omits ground-truth read failure, injection-cap overflow, and unparseable output
Required-input failure path is correctly mapped and verified
